# Fork-maintained patches for rayward-external/litellm
#
# Verified on every push, every PR, and daily on a cron by
# .github/workflows/fork-patch-verify.yml, which runs
# scripts/verify_fork_patches.py against this file -- see that script's
# docstring for the full format contract, match strategy, and why some rows
# are intentionally not checked. Short version:
#
# Format: <file>[ / <file> ...] | <pattern> | <human_description>
#   - <pattern> matched as a literal substring OR a MULTILINE (NOT DOTALL)
#     regex, whichever finds it -- if neither does, the row's patch is
#     treated as reverted/dropped and the check fails. DOTALL was dropped
#     because it let `.` cross newlines, so `FROM.*sha256:` was satisfied by
#     ANY `FROM` plus ANY later `sha256:` in the file: one surviving pinned
#     stage vouched for every other stage, and a per-stage revert passed
#     green. Anchor patterns to a line (`^FROM \S+@sha256:`); if a row must
#     span lines, say so explicitly with `[\s\S]` and temper it so it
#     cannot run past the block it describes.
#   - flipping a live row's pattern to `N/A` silences it. The script pins the
#     N/A count (EXPECTED_NA_ROWS), so doing that fails until the number is
#     raised in the same commit and argued for in review.
#   - <pattern> of exactly `N/A` marks a row with no local greppable artifact
#     (a GitHub-side action, or a row superseded by a later one recording the
#     same fact's current value) -- kept for audit trail, never checked.
#   - a <file> ending in `-budget.json` is a ratchet-log file (ruff-strict,
#     type-discipline, basedpyright-code, test-quality): its rows are a
#     changelog of past hand-raised ceilings, not a claim that stays true --
#     `make lint-budget-update` silently ratchets these down over time with
#     no new row, so a later row's value is routinely LOWER than an earlier
#     one. Not pattern-checked; the ceiling's own currency is enforced by
#     the ratchet gate it describes (scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py and
#     siblings, wired into test-linting.yml), not by this file.
#
# Presence is necessary but NOT sufficient for one class of patch: a literal
# digest pin that shadows an ARG default (below) can stay present while
# drifting to a stale value nothing compares it to -- exactly what broke the
# image build 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-02 (rayward-external/litellm#239). That
# class therefore gets a SECOND phase in the same script rather than a grep
# pattern here: verify_fork_patches.py's dockerfile_pin_failures() compares
# every literal `FROM <image>@sha256:` in every Dockerfile THIS FILE NAMES
# against the `ARG ..._IMAGE` default it shadows -- full reference, name+tag
# +digest -- and fails if they differ, if a required Dockerfile is unnamed or
# missing, or if a required Dockerfile yields zero comparisons (vacuity).
# tests/test_litellm/test_dockerfile_base_image_pins.py is the pytest entry
# point to that same implementation, so a `pytest` run and the daily cron can
# never disagree about what "pinned" means; it also runs phase 1, so the row
# below guarding fork-patch-verify.yml's own existence is no longer checked
# only by the workflow it guards.
#
# Anti-vacuity is asserted per (file, STAGE), not per file
# (EXPECTED_LITERAL_PIN_STAGES): reverting ONE stage to `FROM $VAR` used to
# pass, because the reverted line simply stopped being compared while the
# file's other pins kept it looking covered.
#
# Write pin rows' <pattern> version-AGNOSTICALLY (e.g. `FROM.*sha256:`, not a
# literal digest or `node:20\.18`): phase 1 asserts the pin is PRESENT, phase 2
# asserts it is CURRENT. A row that hardcodes today's version becomes the thing
# that goes stale -- which is how the ui-builder pin sat drifted from
# 2026-08-04 to 2026-09-02 with this file reporting green.

Dockerfile            | ^FROM \S+@sha256: | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM); this is the Dockerfile litellm-build-push.yml deploys (Scorecard PinnedDependenciesID)
backend/Dockerfile    | ^FROM \S+@sha256: | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
gateway/Dockerfile    | ^FROM \S+@sha256: | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
migrations/Dockerfile | ^FROM \S+@sha256: | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
.github/workflows/codeql.yml        | timeout-minutes: 90                       | CodeQL analyze job timeout raised 30->90 min so python leg completes
.github/workflows/codeql.yml        | workflow_dispatch:                        | Added manual-dispatch trigger: PR #260's Analyze (python/javascript-typescript/actions) runs got stuck permanently queued with zero jobs materialized (GitHub Actions scheduling fault), and the run could be neither cancelled nor rerun via the API while it only had push/pull_request/schedule triggers. workflow_dispatch gives a recovery lever to manually re-fire CodeQL against a branch when the automatic trigger wedges like this. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; keep as a standing recovery lever.
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/log-injection                          | Exclude CWE-117 query: taint explosion from pervasive logging; same scaling class as py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data
.github/workflows/fork-patch-verify.yml | verify-fork-patches                | The verifier this whole manifest was missing (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#694): runs scripts/verify_fork_patches.py on every PR and daily so a -X theirs sync that silently drops one of THIS file's own recorded patches fails CI instead of surfacing as a later build break, same class as rayward-external/litellm#239. A directory-level -X theirs resolution of .github/workflows/ can wipe fork-only new files in that dir wholesale, same risk as alert-bridge.yml below; re-apply this workflow (and scripts/verify_fork_patches.py) if a sync drops them. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this IS the sync-CI condition AGENTS.md's cost-tracking exception depends on.
scripts/verify_fork_patches.py | def parse_manifest                     | Companion script to the row above -- parses this file and checks every current-assertion row's pattern is still present. Same wipe risk as any fork-only file under a directory the upstream sync also touches. REMOVAL CONDITION: none.

Also added per-alert file:line output to the list mode's step summary.

litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/litellm_content_filter/content_filter.py | resolved category file path escapes the category data roots | _load_categories: containment re-check on category_file_path immediately before use, closing py/path-injection (#1025) as defense-in-depth alongside the existing category_name regex validation. CodeQL (PR #182) flagged this same rule again on 2026-08-04: the containment check validated real_category_file_path but the subsequent os.path.exists()/_load_category_file() sinks still read the unsanitized category_file_path, so the taint path through the un-normalized variable was never actually closed. Both sinks now take real_category_file_path. CodeQL (alerts #1116-1118) flagged it a third time on 2026-10-02's sync: that fix had narrowed the containment check to the primary CATEGORIES_DIR alone, so any legitimate result from the dual-root search (LEGACY_DATA_DIR, added by the same sync) was rejected as an escape -- loaded_categories came back empty, caught by TestLegacyPackageRootStaysSearchable (3 failures). Now checks every root in the function's own `roots` parameter, via a non-realpath-following normpath comparison (not is_within, which follows symlinks and would reject a symlink placed inside a root -- the exact case find_category_file's own join_within is designed to trust). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream applies an equivalent containment check.

Dockerfile        | FROM --platform=\$BUILDPLATFORM node:\S+@sha256: | (ui-builder stage) Literal digest pin for the ui-builder stage (was ARG-variable FROM \$UI_BUILD_IMAGE), closing PinnedDependencies #1009/#1020. Same pattern as the other stages in this file. The pattern is deliberately version-AGNOSTIC: this row asserts the pin is PRESENT, while whether it is CURRENT is phase 2's job (scripts/verify_fork_patches.py compares it to ARG UI_BUILD_IMAGE). Pinning a literal node version here instead would make the row itself the thing that goes stale -- which is how this pin sat drifted at node:20.18-alpine3.20 from 2026-08-04 (upstream commit 487074f602 moved ARG UI_BUILD_IMAGE to node:24.19-alpine3.24) until phase 2's first run caught it, with the manifest reporting green the whole time. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream pins this stage itself.

docker/Dockerfile.non_root            | FROM ghcr\.io/astral-sh/uv:0\.11\.7@sha256:   | Literal digest pin for uvbin/ui-builder stages (were ARG-variable FROM), closing PinnedDependencies #1013/#1014. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream pins these stages itself.
tests/test_litellm/test_dockerfile_base_image_pins.py | test_no_stale_literal_from_pins | Regression guard for every literal digest pin above. The RULE now lives in scripts/verify_fork_patches.py (dockerfile_pin_failures) so it also runs on the daily fork-patch-verify.yml schedule and after every upstream sync, not only when this suite happens to run (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#694); this module is the pytest entry point to that same implementation and imports it by path, so the two can never disagree. Asserts each Dockerfile's literal `FROM <image>@sha256:` still equals the `ARG ..._IMAGE` default it shadows -- full reference, name+tag+digest -- and that the patched files still carry both. A literal pin is not a variable reference, so an upstream ARG bump leaves it behind with nothing comparing the two. That drift broke the image build on 2026-08-30: upstream moved the ARG to a wolfi-base with glibc 2.44 and switched to `apk add python-3.13` / `uv sync --python python3.13`, the literal FROM lines stayed on a May 2026 wolfi-base with glibc 2.43, and the build died with "/usr/lib/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.44' not found". The FIRST version of this guard was keyed on an allowlist of two image repos (wolfi-base, astral-sh/uv) and compared digests only, so it stayed green for a month while the ui-builder stage of Dockerfile, docker/Dockerfile.database and docker/Dockerfile.non_root sat on node:20.18-alpine3.20 after upstream commit 487074f602 (2026-08-04) moved ARG UI_BUILD_IMAGE to node:24.19-alpine3.24 -- fixed by generalizing the rule to every pinned image and re-pinning all three. Covers Dockerfile, backend/, gateway/, migrations/, docker/Dockerfile.database (REQUIRED_PINNED_DOCKERFILES) and opportunistically docker/Dockerfile.non_root. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this is the not-stale half of the sync-CI condition AGENTS.md's cost-tracking exception depends on.

litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py | _translate_legacy_thinking_for_adaptive_model | Fork-only legacy thinking.enabled -> adaptive translation (infers an output_config.effort from the legacy budget_tokens, so pre-existing budget_tokens-based callers keep working on adaptive-thinking models) plus its _legacy_thinking_budget_to_effort/_coerce_optional_int helpers and the transform_request call site. Every -X theirs sync so far has silently dropped this (restored three times now: commit 343d3008, the 2026-07-12 sync, and the 2026-07-16 sync); it never conflicts textually with upstream's edits to the surrounding transform_request body, so git's 3-way merge just drops it instead of flagging a conflict. Signatures must be re-checked against upstream's current _is_adaptive_thinking_model/_validate_effort_for_model signatures each time (upstream has added a custom_llm_provider parameter to both since this was first written) — do not copy-paste the old diff verbatim. 2026-09-03 sync: upstream shipped its own AnthropicModelInfo.translate_legacy_thinking_for_adaptive_model (litellm/llms/anthropic/common_utils.py), now the shared cross-surface translator called from map_openai_params's `elif param == "thinking":` else-branch AND from Bedrock invoke/converse, Databricks, and Vertex, ahead of this file's own transform_request call site. Upstream's version was not a full equivalent -- its _legacy_budget_to_effort topped out at "xhigh" with no "max" tier for the budget_tokens>=max_tokens case this file's _legacy_thinking_budget_to_effort handles -- but it still rewrites optional_params["thinking"]["type"] to "adaptive" before transform_request runs, so this file's own translator's `thinking.get("type") != "enabled"` guard short-circuits and the richer mapping never fires (caught by test_legacy_thinking_enabled_translates_to_max_adaptive_for_opus_48_chat: asserted "max", got "high"). Simply removing the new map_openai_params call (an earlier commit on this PR tried that) restores this file's own translator as sole path but breaks test_legacy_thinking_translated_to_adaptive_on_adaptive_only_models, which calls map_openai_params directly and depends on IT performing the /chat/completions translation without a transform_request call following it. Ported the max_tokens-aware "max" tier into the shared common_utils.py helper instead (kept the map_openai_params call site intact), so every surface gets the same effort mapping and both test files pass. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove this row's max_tokens-aware branch once upstream's own shared helper grows the "max" tier itself.
litellm/proxy/response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py | @router\.websocket\("/v1/responses"\) | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650): Responses API WebSocket mode is RE-ENABLED — the @router.websocket("/v1/responses") and @router.websocket("/responses") decorators on responses_websocket_endpoint, removed 2026-08-27 by #214 (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#645) because every non-Vertex leg failed after the upgrade, are restored now that the three root causes are fixed by the backports below (BerriAI/litellm#34253, #33101, #33463). tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_proxy_routes.py's guard was inverted from test_responses_api_does_not_register_websocket_mode to test_responses_api_registers_websocket_mode (now asserts the WebSocket route IS registered on both aliases) and tests/openai_endpoints_tests/test_responses_websocket_proxy_e2e.py's skip mark was dropped; ui/litellm-dashboard/src/lib/http/schema.d.ts had the two websocket operations restored. litellm/responses/main.py | or api_key | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650, #645): _aresponses_websocket's resolved_api_key must stay `None` for a Bedrock/Vertex/SageMaker-style deployment, exactly like the HTTP path leaves litellm_params.api_key at `None` for those providers (litellm/main.py's bedrock dispatch never resolves an api_key at all: "boto3 reads keys from .env"). Upstream BerriAI/litellm#34253 (still OPEN) added `or api_key` ahead of a `litellm.api_key or litellm.openai_key or get_secret_str("OPENAI_API_KEY")` tail, which was necessary (it preserves an explicit caller-supplied key) but NOT sufficient: a Bedrock deployment with no api_key of its own still fell all the way through that tail to OPENAI_API_KEY, and base_aws_llm.py's get_request_headers treats ANY non-None api_key as an AWS bearer token, bypassing SigV4 and raising "Invalid API Key format: Must start with pre-defined prefix" (measured live against gateway.rayward.ai 2026-08-27, reproducing #645's original symptom). Fixed by dropping the cross-provider secret-store tail entirely: resolved_api_key is now `dynamic_api_key or api_key or litellm_params.api_key`, matching the HTTP path's litellm_params.api_key exactly, so each provider's own config/completion() branch resolves its own credentials or fallback (as OpenAI's validate_environment already does) instead of a generic OpenAI key racing in ahead of them. Guarded by tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_websocket_all_providers.py::TestResponsesAPIWebSocketSupport::test_bedrock_websocket_does_not_leak_openai_key_as_bearer_token. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop when upstream BerriAI/litellm#34253 (or an equivalent fix) merges and a sync absorbs it.
litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | call_kwargs\["proxy_server_request"\]\s*= | backport of upstream BerriAI/litellm#33101 (OPEN, "fix(responses): stop managed Responses WebSocket from leaking litellm_params into provider request body", rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650): ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler._update_proxy_request nested proxy_server_request under call_kwargs["litellm_params"], and litellm_params is not a Responses API request field, so strict providers (e.g. Anthropic) rejected the forwarded call with "litellm_params: Extra inputs are not permitted". Fixed by setting call_kwargs["proxy_server_request"] directly instead of nesting it under a synthesized litellm_params dict. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop when upstream BerriAI/litellm#33101 merges and a sync absorbs it.
litellm/responses/main.py | _build_responses_websocket_request_defaults | backport of upstream BerriAI/litellm#33463 (OPEN, "fix(responses): apply deployment defaults to websocket frames", rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650): deployment-level defaults (reasoning effort, service_tier, extra_body provider params) passed to responses() were never threaded through to WebSocket response.create frames, so a WebSocket session silently dropped the caller's per-deployment configuration that the HTTP path honors. Adds _build_responses_websocket_request_defaults (litellm/responses/main.py) to collect those defaults, threads them as request_defaults through BaseLLMHTTPHandler.async_responses_websocket (litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py) and ResponsesWebSocketStreaming (litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py), which merges them into each response.create frame via the new _apply_request_defaults, filling in only keys the client did not already set. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop when upstream BerriAI/litellm#33463 merges and a sync absorbs it.
litellm/responses/main.py | custom_llm_provider=litellm_params.custom_llm_provider | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650): _aresponses_websocket's litellm.get_llm_provider(...) call ignored the router-resolved custom_llm_provider already sitting in kwargs and re-derived the provider from the bare model string alone. Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry and Vertex deployments deliberately configure a BARE litellm_params.model (no "azure/"/"azure_ai/"/"vertex_ai/" prefix) and rely entirely on the separate custom_llm_provider field for routing (gcp/modules/gateway_cloud_run/litellm.config.yaml.tmpl in llm-gateway-infra: "Keep model_name and litellm_params.model bare"). Re-deriving from "gpt-5.5" alone silently matched litellm's own OpenAI model-name heuristic, producing custom_llm_provider="openai" and OpenAIResponsesAPIConfig instead of Azure's — an OpenAI-shaped request against an Azure api_base, which Azure answered with `OpenAIException - 404 Resource not found` (measured live 2026-08-27, matching #650's Azure WS-bridge row). A bare "kimi-k2.6" (Azure AI Foundry) matches no heuristic at all, so the same re-derivation raised an uncaught `litellm.BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided` before a single WebSocket frame was ever sent — measured live as "no frames at all". Fixed by passing the already-resolved litellm_params.custom_llm_provider into get_llm_provider, mirroring the `if custom_llm_provider is None` gate aresponses()/responses() already use on the HTTP path. Guarded by tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_websocket_all_providers.py::TestResponsesAPIWebSocketSupport::test_azure_websocket_honors_router_resolved_custom_llm_provider and ::test_azure_ai_foundry_websocket_does_not_crash_on_bare_model_name. REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; this is a fork-local WS/HTTP parity fix — remove only if _aresponses_websocket is rewritten to resolve the provider a different way that still honors an already-known custom_llm_provider.
litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py | falling back to the managed bridge | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650, #645): a native-WebSocket-capable provider (OpenAI, Azure) whose deployment does not actually expose a working wss:// Responses endpoint used to close the CLIENT's already-accepted WebSocket with code 1011 when the upstream handshake failed, because websockets 15.x raises InvalidStatus on a rejected handshake, not the deprecated InvalidStatusCode the old except clause caught, so it fell straight into the generic except-and-close branch (measured live against an Azure OpenAI deployment 2026-08-27: our gateway sends the client its 101, then the connection closes with code 1011, reason "server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 404", reproducing #645's "HTTP 404 during connection" row). Fixed by entering the native backend connection through an AsyncExitStack and catching the handshake step's failure separately: on ANY exception establishing the upstream socket, async_responses_websocket now instantiates ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler (the same HTTP-backed bridge every non-native provider, e.g. Fireworks and Vertex, already uses successfully) instead of closing the client connection, since the client has not received a single frame yet and bridging is strictly better. Guarded by tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_websocket_all_providers.py::TestNativeWebSocketUrlConstruction::test_native_websocket_handshake_failure_falls_back_to_managed_bridge. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop once our Azure/OpenAI Cloud Run deployments genuinely expose a working wss:// Responses endpoint end-to-end and this fallback path is provably dead, or once upstream ships an equivalent fallback itself.

litellm/proxy/common_utils/budget_window_headers.py | def format_budget_windows | feature (#481, reshaped #491): renders a key's CONCURRENT budget windows (1d/1w/1mo) into x-usage-budget. Broker keys set `budget_limits`, never top-level `max_budget`, so get_custom_headers read None -> "None" -> dropped by exclude_values, and the header NEVER shipped to an external caller. Carries `spent` alongside `limit` per window because x-usage-spend is LIFETIME and cannot be subtracted from a windowed cap (a fourth header was declined, owner 2026-08-02). #491 MOVED THE HEADER NAME: BUDGET_HEADER_NAME is now the fork-only `x-litellm-key-budget-windows`, NOT upstream's `x-litellm-key-max-budget`. Overloading the upstream name put two value types under it, which no reader can dispatch on — the fork's own gateway_cost.py did float(raw) and silently reported max_budget:None for every windowed key. NEUTRAL_BUDGET_HEADER_NAME ("x-usage-budget") is exported beside it so the guards can assert both halves. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop if upstream ever publishes per-window budgets itself. #491 FOLLOW-UP: format_budget_windows also COLLAPSES same-duration windows to the least-remaining one. The published format is a list keyed by window name and the customer-facing parser turns it into a dict, so two entries sharing a duration silently overwrite each other — and the later assignment wins, so the LOOSER cap survives and headroom is overstated. The sibling gateway shipped exactly this (1d;limit=1000 beside 1d;limit=5000 reported $4999.89 of headroom against a real $999.99 cap). Duplicates are not configured here today, but budget_limits is an iterated LIST not a mapping, so it is one config edit away. Do not simplify this back to a plain join.
litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py | valid_token.budget_window_usage | feature (#481) — THE SOURCE. _virtual_key_multi_budget_check already reads every window's counter (it is the enforcement); this stashes what it read so the sync get_custom_headers can publish it without a second cache round-trip and without disagreeing with the numbers enforcement acted on. Losing this line leaves the formatter correct and the header empty — silent.
litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py | format_budget_windows(getattr | feature (#481, extended #491) — THE WIRING, tracked separately because losing it is silent and the formatter's own tests stay green. There are now TWO format_budget_windows call sites and they are not interchangeable: one fills the NEUTRAL `x-usage-budget` (for internal callers — the external allowlist drops it by design), the other fills the fork-only branded twin `x-litellm-key-budget-windows` that the external rename table reads. Losing either silently blinds exactly one audience. The same patch emits `x-usage-cost` / `x-usage-spend` at source so the documented contract works on the internal hostname too, and RESTORES upstream's `"x-litellm-key-max-budget": str(user_api_key_dict.max_budget)` — do not re-add the `or str(...)` overload a sync may suggest. NOTE the getattr: direct attribute access would raise AttributeError on EVERY request if the _types.py half is reverted by a sync, and breaks upstream tests that build MagicMock(spec=UserAPIKeyAuth) since pydantic v2 fields are invisible to a mock spec. Both were observed 2026-08-02. The wiring guards assert over the AST, not source text, because ruff format reflows these calls.
litellm/proxy/_types.py | budget_window_usage | feature (#481): transient per-request field on UserAPIKeyAuth holding the window snapshot, exclude=True like the neighbouring budget_reservation — never persisted, never part of the key's API shape.
litellm/proxy/middleware/external_audience_middleware.py | RENAMED_HEADERS | security (#441/#443/#487, retuned #491) — the ENTIRE external-audience response policy, and it had no manifest entry until #491. A strict ALLOWLIST plus a three-entry rename table; losing it exposes x-litellm-* (names our gateway software), llm_provider-* (proves we proxy, carries upstream request ids) and bare x-ratelimit-* (OUR purchased quota) to external parties. THE RENAME IS THE ONLY WAY A NEUTRAL NAME REACHES AN EXTERNAL CALLER and that is load-bearing, not tidiable: the neutral names are deliberately absent from ALLOWED_HEADERS so a source-emitted copy (#491 emits all three internally) and a hostile upstream copy on the pass-through path both die at the boundary, leaving exactly one value. Allowlisting any neutral name forfeits that. The budget entry reads the fork-only `x-litellm-key-budget-windows`, never upstream's `x-litellm-key-max-budget` — renaming the latter would publish `None` for every windowed key. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this is ours permanently.
litellm/constants.py | "x-usage-cost", | feature (#491): appends the three neutral usage names to LITELLM_UI_ALLOW_HEADERS, which proxy_server.py passes to CORSMiddleware as expose_headers. Emitting a response header is NOT enough for a cross-origin browser caller — a browser returns null from response.headers for any name absent from that list, with no error raised, so the loss is silent. Internal callers only; the external middleware REPLACES access-control-expose-headers with the neutral names because this list advertises literal x-litellm-* names and is itself a disclosure. Found by review, not by a test: the suite drives the app in-process where CORS never runs. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop if upstream ever exposes these itself.

enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/common_utils/check_batch_cost.py | attribution = self._get_job_attribution(job) | 2026-08-21 sync merge corruption, round 3 (same recurring class as the 2026-08-09/2026-08-14/2026-08-15 entries above): upstream independently grew its own second job-claim layer this cycle (_claim_job_for_costing / _release_job_claim, called from inside _track_completed_batch_cost right before the spend-log write) alongside the fork's pre-existing layer (_claim_job / _release_job_claim / _finalize_job, called from check_batch_cost before _track_completed_batch_cost even runs). Both additions land in disjoint hunks, so the merge auto-applied both with no conflict, silently producing two claim layers stacked on the same row: the outer _claim_job flips batch_processed=True before the inner _claim_job_for_costing runs, so the inner claim's own compare-and-swap (where batch_processed=False) always finds 0 rows and _track_completed_batch_cost always returns None without ever calling async_success_handler -- batches stop being billed at all, and the row is left oscillating between claim and release every poll cycle. Also silently shadowed: Python keeps only the LAST definition of a duplicate method name, so the fork's fenced _release_job_claim(status="pricing") was shadowed by upstream's simpler unfenced one, meaning the release path stopped restoring status to "validating" too. Fixed by deleting upstream's newly-added _claim_job_for_costing method, its duplicate _release_job_claim definition, and the wrapping claim-check/try-release-on-exception it added around the async_success_handler call in _track_completed_batch_cost, restoring this file to byte-identical with the pre-sync commit for this whole region. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; regression fix. Separately, NOT fixed by this patch: upstream's new claim timing (claim right before the spend-log write, after the results fetch) exists specifically because claiming earlier -- which is what the fork's _claim_job still does, unchanged since before this sync -- flips batch_processed=True before the output file has been read, and the managed-files deletion guard treats batch_processed=True as "safe to delete," so a concurrent delete can remove the very output file an in-flight costing run is reading. This is a real, pre-existing gap in the fork's design (not introduced by this sync) that tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_check_batch_cost.py::TestMultiPodBatchCostClaim (upstream's brand-new test class this cycle) catches; closing it requires moving the fork's claim point later while preserving its status="pricing" fencing, _reclaim_abandoned_pricing_claims sweep, and spend-already-recorded dedup marker, none of which upstream's simpler single-flag claim provides, so it is a deliberate follow-up, not part of this merge-corruption fix. REMOVAL CONDITION: track upstream's job-claim/locking layer maturity as in the 2026-08-09 entry above; additionally, reconcile the claim-timing gap once a deliberate redesign of the fork's claim point is scoped and reviewed.
litellm/proxy/prisma_migration.py | LITELLM_PRISMA_CLIENT_PREBAKED | Skips the standalone entrypoint's own runtime `prisma generate` when set. Genuine upstream breakage, confirmed present on a clean upstream checkout (Dockerfile, docker/Dockerfile.non_root, and prisma_migration.py are all byte-identical to upstream/litellm_internal_staging): upstream's own PR #37692 (merged into this fork by the 2026-08-21 sync) made the entrypoint return prisma generate's exit code by default instead of only logging it, turning a previously-silent failure into a hard one. prisma-python's generator.generate() unconditionally re-copies schema.prisma into the installed package and chmod's the copy even when the content already matches (prisma/generator/generator.py compares paths, not bytes), and shutil.copy's chmod step (copymode) requires owning the destination file -- something no arbitrary non-root runtime uid does for a file baked into the image at build time, no matter how the image's permissions are set up. The runtime images already bake the generated client from this same schema.prisma at build time, so re-running generate at container start is pure redundant work; skipping it removes the only place that redundant call is made (migrations/run.py's ProxyExtrasDBManager never calls it). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream either stops re-running `prisma generate` in this entrypoint for prebaked images, or prisma-python skips schema.prisma re-copy/chmod when the destination already matches.

enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/common_utils/check_batch_cost.py | Called from _track_completed_batch_cost | 2026-08-22 resolution of the claim-timing gap left open by the 2026-08-21 entry above. The fork claimed a row before fetching its results, which flipped batch_processed=True while the output file was still being read. Two consequences, both real: the managed-files deletion guard (_get_batches_referencing_file filters batch_processed=False) stopped holding the output file, so a concurrent delete could remove the very file the in-flight costing was reading; and a worker killed mid-fetch left the batch marked processed, unbillable by any other pod until _reclaim_abandoned_pricing_claims swept it hours later. Moved the claim to where upstream's own claim sits, inside _track_completed_batch_cost immediately before logging_obj.async_success_handler, WITHOUT adopting upstream's simpler single-flag claim: the fork's status="pricing" fencing, _reclaim_abandoned_pricing_claims sweep, _mark_spend_recorded dedup marker and fenced _finalize_job are all retained, so the crash-re-billing and disable_spend_logs protections they provide are unchanged. Losing the compare-and-swap now costs only a duplicated results fetch (the winner bills exactly once) and is signalled to the caller by the CLAIM_LOST sentinel, distinct from the unroutable-row None. Callers that previously released a claim they held across the fetch no longer do so: a failed fetch never took a claim and leaves the row untouched outright, while a failed spend-log write releases inside _track_completed_batch_cost. tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_check_batch_cost.py::TestMultiPodBatchCostClaim (upstream's class) now passes; its journal and claim-call assertions were adapted to the fork's write shape (claim carries status="pricing"; the marker and fenced finalize are separate writes) while every behavioural assertion upstream makes is kept. REMOVAL CONDITION: track upstream's job-claim/locking layer maturity as in the 2026-08-09 entry above; the claim-timing divergence itself is now closed, so only the extra fencing/sweep/marker remain fork-only.

It DOES break cross-connection TPM/RPM enforcement: the active rate limiter, _PROXY_MaxParallelRequestsHandler_v3 (litellm/proxy/hooks/parallel_request_limiter_v3.py:4157), reads standard_logging_object["metadata"]["user_api_key_hash"] to attribute a turn's tokens to the right counter, and that field is NOT protected by get_litellm_metadata_from_kwargs's merge -- so a colliding client metadata object silently dropped usage attribution from the counter the rate limiter reads (litellm_params["metadata"] is what standard_logging_object construction reads from -- verified deterministically with a real registered success callback, tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_websocket_all_providers.py::TestWebSocketProxyIdentityMetadataMerge; the further end-to-end claim that this alone makes a subsequent connection's pre_call_hook reject was attempted against the real _PROXY_MaxParallelRequestsHandler_v3 + real InternalUsageCache but could not be reproduced reliably -- its reservation/correction accounting behaved inconsistently across runs in ways not fully root-caused, so that specific claim is NOT asserted by a test; see TestWebSocketRateLimitEnforcementMechanism's docstring for the retraction and the static mechanism trace that does hold). Fixed by folding the caller's metadata under litellm_metadata (as "requester_metadata", mirroring add_litellm_data_to_request's own convention for the HTTP path) instead of leaving it as a colliding top-level kwarg. Scope: this fixes non-native providers only (anything routed through ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler -- Fireworks, Vertex, Bedrock-Mantle, etc.). Native providers (Azure, OpenAI) take a completely different code path (ResponsesWebSocketStreaming) with its own, separately-tracked usage-accounting gap (dispatches an entire connection's raw WS event list to the logging pipeline once at connection close instead of per-turn from a proper response object -- tracked as a follow-up on its own branch, not fixed here). REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; this is a fork-local WS/proxy-hook correctness fix protecting a proxy-internal contract (standard_logging_object metadata shape) that has no upstream equivalent to converge on. Remove only if ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler's per-turn call construction is redesigned in a way that no longer risks this collision.
litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | RESPONSES_WS_TERMINAL_EVENT_CLASSES | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#657, owner-approved 2026-08-28 as a governance fix, NOT a candidate for silent removal on sync): ResponsesWebSocketStreaming (the NATIVE-provider WS bridge used when responses_api_provider_config.supports_native_websocket() is True -- Azure, OpenAI; a raw bidirectional proxy between client and upstream, distinct from ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler) used to dispatch cost/usage exactly once per CONNECTION, in backend_to_client's finally: block at connection close, via _log_messages() calling self.logging_obj.dispatch_success_handlers(self.messages, ...) where self.messages is a raw Python list of stored WS event dicts. _get_assembled_streaming_response (litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py:3670-3693) has no branch for a bare list and returns None before any cost/usage is computed, so response_cost and total_tokens always came out 0/0.0 regardless of real usage. Confirmed against production: a live DB query against LiteLLM_SpendLogs for the 2026-08-28 04:00-04:45 UTC window found 11 _aresponses_websocket rows (one per WebSocket session, all model=gpt-5.6-sol/azure) against 200+ response.completed frames in the same window -- one row per SESSION, every row spend=0, total_tokens=prompt_tokens=completion_tokens=0, status='success' (written as zero, not skipped) -- exactly the "one row per connection, always zero" shape this bug predicts. Fixed by, as each response.completed/response.failed/response.incomplete frame is forwarded (inside backend_to_client's loop, not at connection close), parsing it into the correctly-typed ResponseCompletedEvent/ResponseFailedEvent/ResponseIncompleteEvent and dispatching it on a FRESH per-turn LiteLLMLoggingObj via _build_per_turn_logging_obj/_dispatch_turn_cost. This lands on _get_assembled_streaming_response's EXISTING correct branch for those three types (:3672-3673) -- no logging-layer change needed. A fresh logging_obj per turn is not optional: verified by running (not reading) that reusing one shared Logging(stream=True) instance across multiple dispatch_success_handlers calls silently drops every turn after the first, because the dedup guard model_call_details["has_dispatched_final_stream_success"] is keyed on the logging_obj instance. _log_messages() (the old close-time hook) no longer dispatches anything -- only sets model_call_details["messages"] for input-trace bookkeeping -- so the fix does not double-count against it. Row cardinality changes deliberately from one row per session to one row per turn; verified safe because SpendLogs' primary key (get_spend_logs_id, litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py:190-201) prefers the response's own `id` over litellm_call_id, and every real provider response.completed event carries a genuinely distinct response id per turn (this fix also generates an independent fresh litellm_call_id per turn as a second source of uniqueness) -- see test_distinct_turns_get_distinct_request_ids. requester_ip_address (blank on every pre-fix WS spend row, per the same production query) is a side-effect improvement: the fresh per-turn metadata dict copies self.request_data["litellm_metadata"] verbatim, which add_litellm_data_to_request already populates with requester_ip_address at connection setup -- verified it threads through correctly (test_turn_cost_attributes_to_the_correct_key). Cost/usage read the ALREADY output-masked event string (same one forwarded to the client), so a PII-masked text block is never billed differently and masking never races ahead of or behind what gets costed (test_turn_cost_unaffected_by_output_pii_masking). SCOPE: this is forward-only. The 11+ zero-valued spend rows already written for past sessions are NOT backfilled or corrected by this change -- per-turn usage for those sessions is unrecoverable from the DB (it only ever existed in the forwarded WS frames, never persisted), and any historical correction is an owner decision touching production data, not something this patch attempts. REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; this is a fork-local correctness fix for a code path (ResponsesWebSocketStreaming) with no upstream WS-mode cost-accounting equivalent to converge on. Remove only if this class's per-turn dispatch mechanism is redesigned in a way that no longer risks the once-per-connection/raw-list regression.
litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | self._pending_cost_tasks | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#657, owner-approved 2026-08-28, part of the same native-path usage-accounting fix above -- NOT a candidate for silent removal on sync): the per-turn cost dispatch tasks _dispatch_turn_cost creates (asyncio.create_task(...)) were fire-and-forget -- no reference retained, and bidirectional_forward's finally: cancelled/awaited only the forward_task and closed backend_ws, never touching the cost tasks. Two distinct exposures, caught on review before landing: (1) asyncio's own documentation is explicit that the event loop holds only a WEAK reference to a bare create_task() result, so a task whose result is not retained anywhere can be garbage-collected mid-execution; (2) even with a strong reference, returning from bidirectional_forward without waiting on them risks losing an in-flight dispatch to instance teardown -- concretely, Cloud Run scaling the instance down after the connection ends (we run on Cloud Run and scale to zero) or a deploy/restart killing in-flight tasks; the realistic trigger is narrower than "the event loop stops" (uvicorn's loop keeps running other connections, so a pending task usually completes in practice), but not hypothetical, and it targets the worst possible turn: a client disconnecting right after its final response.completed leaves the LAST (often largest) turn of every session with the least time to flush. Fixed by retaining every created task in self._pending_cost_tasks (populated in _dispatch_turn_cost, discarded via add_done_callback) and draining it with a BOUNDED wait in a new _drain_pending_cost_tasks method, called from bidirectional_forward's finally: after forward_task is done (so no new tasks can still be added). The bound reuses LOGGING_WORKER_MAX_TIME_PER_COROUTINE (litellm/constants.py) -- the same env-overridable per-coroutine budget the SDK already applies to one logging dispatch via GLOBAL_LOGGING_WORKER -- rather than a new bespoke constant, and exists specifically so a hung callback (a stuck DB write, a slow webhook) can never wedge connection teardown. Also: _dispatch_turn_cost's JSON-parse-failure branch (a terminal frame that fails to even parse) now logs at WARNING instead of returning silently -- a terminal frame this code cannot parse is a silently unbilled turn, the exact failure class this whole issue is about, and it must be visible rather than repeating the original bug in a new place. Guarded by TestNativeWebSocketPerTurnCostAccounting::test_pending_cost_tasks_hold_strong_references, ::test_drain_waits_for_a_turn_dispatched_just_before_teardown (asserts with NO extra sleep after the drain call -- a test that slept afterward would pass whether or not the drain exists) and ::test_bidirectional_forward_drains_pending_cost_tasks_before_returning. REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; fork-local task-ownership fix for a fork-local per-turn dispatch mechanism with no upstream equivalent. Remove only if the per-turn dispatch is redesigned to no longer create ad hoc tasks (e.g. an awaited, ordered dispatch instead of fire-and-forget).

litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | def _flatten_response_create | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#689): the NATIVE Responses WS bridge (ResponsesWebSocketStreaming, used when responses_api_provider_config.supports_native_websocket() is True -- Azure, OpenAI) is a literal pass-through to the provider's own /v1/responses socket, so whatever client_to_backend sends is what the provider sees. The OpenAI-documented NESTED response.create shape ({"type":"response.create","response":{...}}) was forwarded verbatim and rejected upstream with "missing_required_parameter: 'input'" on EVERY turn, making the bridge unusable for a conformant client. _mask_response_create's helpers (_apply_request_defaults, _enforce_authorized_model) each read and write INSIDE the nested envelope and were documented as "handles both shapes", but neither ever hoisted those fields back to the top level or dropped the "response" key -- _apply_request_defaults explicitly rebinds msg_obj["response"] = request -- so nested went in nested and came out nested; there was no flattening step anywhere on this path. Fixed by _flatten_response_create, called FIRST in _mask_response_create (the single point every client frame passes through, for both the first_message and the receive loop), which deletes the envelope and hoists its keys to the top level; nested values win over a same-named top-level key and the envelope's own stray "type" never overwrites the client event type. Every later step (defaults merge, authorized-model enforcement, PII masking of input/instructions, _collect_input_from_client_event's flat-only input logging) therefore operates on the flat frame that is actually sent -- authorized-model enforcement on the nested shape is asserted by test_mask_response_create_nested_still_enforces_authorized_model, and the frame written to the backend socket by test_client_to_backend_forwards_flattened_frame. Those helpers keep their own nested branches as dead-but-harmless defence. The MANAGED bridge is unaffected: _build_base_call_kwargs already collapses both shapes before calling litellm.aresponses. Evidence for "flat is what the provider wants" is the live measurement recorded on #689 (2026-09-02, llm.rayward.ai, gpt-5.6-luna: flat -> response.created + response.incomplete; nested -> upstream 400 / no response.created), NOT a reading of our own source. NOT FIXED HERE, still open: backend_to_client swallows a backend ConnectionClosed at debug level and never signals the client, so an upstream rejection that arrives as a bare close (rather than an "error" data frame) presents to the caller as a silent hang -- see #689's trace comment. REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; upstream has no equivalent normalization on this path. Remove only if the native bridge stops being a verbatim pass-through, or if the provider begins accepting the nested envelope (re-probe before believing that).

litellm/__init__.py / litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py / litellm/proxy/common_utils/sse_keepalive.py | stream_max_upstream_idle_seconds | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#688), second and independent trigger alongside the stream_stalled_write_timeout_seconds patch from rayward-external/litellm#243: that per-write deadline can only fire when the peer applies backpressure, and the measurement on this deployment's serving path showed the terminating proxy in front of the app does not propagate any. It buffered ~2.0 MB and kept accepting the container's writes while the real client had read nothing for 420s, so every keepalive ping succeeded, no write ever stalled, and the deadline was structurally unreachable (the orphaned production requests' byte counter kept advancing at 2.174 B/s -- ~170 SUCCESSFUL writes, max gap ~16s -- for the ~2,830s after the client left). The same join also reframed the population: 29 of 33 delivered under 4,746 total wire bytes across 555-884s against ~5.5 KB/s for a healthy stream, i.e. hung upstreams producing essentially nothing, not truncated long answers. litellm.stream_max_upstream_idle_seconds therefore caps CONSECUTIVE UPSTREAM SILENCE rather than client stall or total duration. It ships OFF (default None) and this repo's config renders the operating value: the mechanism is general but the number is a statement about one deployment's own traffic, and a tuned constant baked into a world-readable fork would end streams for every operator who never asked (fork-vanilla rule): _keepalive_ping_stream already knows exactly when the upstream is idle, so the cap is measured on the gap between two keepalive pings and only real upstream output restamps it -- a ping is our own byte and deliberately does not, or the cap could never be reached on the one stream shape it exists for. Time the wrapper spends suspended at its own yield is excluded too, so a slow reader stays the write deadline's business. Ends the stream with a terminal Anthropic `error` event (anthropic_upstream_idle_sse_chunk) so an attached client can tell truncation from completion, and tears down through the existing generator cleanup, which refunds the budget reservation when no provider output was ever delivered and bills the partial when some was. Consulted only on the /v1/messages SSE path, which is narrower than the measured population: /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions build their SSE response through create_response directly, not through the keepalive wrapper, so the same near-zero-content rows on those routes are NOT covered by this. Deliberately does NOT touch the passthrough byte relay (raw upstream bytes, no frame of ours to splice) or the A2A caller (JSON-RPC over SSE, different error shape), both of which leave it off. Guarded by tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_sse_keepalive.py (cap fires, pings do not reset it, a slow-but-alive upstream survives, a slow consumer is not counted as upstream silence) and tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_v1_messages_client_stall.py (end-to-end over the real /v1/messages ASGI path, plus both refund branches and coexistence with the write deadline). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream ships an equivalent upstream-idle bound for SSE streams, or once the deployment's frontend propagates client backpressure to the container and the write deadline alone suffices (re-measure before believing either). REVISED (review round 2, rayward-external/litellm#247), three defects in the first shape of this patch, all of them the cap measuring or reporting something other than what it claims: (1) the wait before each deadline check was a whole ping interval, so a cap BELOW the ping cadence was silently rounded up to it -- a 1s cap on the shipped 15s cadence fired at ~15s and the configured value was not an upper bound at all; the wait is now min(next ping, remaining idle deadline), with the ping cadence kept on its own next_ping_at clock so shortening the wait cannot change how often a ping goes out. (2) the wrapper sits on the PROCESSED stream, above the post-call hook chain, and a guardrail configured with streaming_buffer_until_moderated consumes a healthy upstream continuously while deliberately yielding nothing until its end-of-stream scan passes -- so a long buffered response read as upstream silence and was killed. Fixed by measuring the provider rather than what reaches the wrapper: UpstreamStreamMonitor is created only when the cap will actually arm (upstream_stream_monitor_for), _UpstreamActivityStamper relays the raw provider iterator immediately below the hook chain and stamps every chunk on it, and the idle window now runs from the LATER of that stamp and the wrapper's own restamp -- which keeps the two pinned invariants intact, since a ping still never restamps and a consumer suspended at a yield is still not charged to the upstream. The refuse-to-arm-when-buffering fallback was NOT taken: it would ship a cap that any buffering guardrail silently disables, and the stamp is ~15 lines confined to one call site. (3) firing the cap closed the data generator, whose cancellation path unconditionally set client_disconnected, recorded 499 and dispatched partial-stream success logging -- so the client got a timeout event while the logs and callbacks reported a client disconnect. The monitor carries that termination back down instead (ended_by_upstream_idle); see the sibling row for the metadata/status half. Refund and partial-billing behaviour is unchanged in both directions: no provider output -> reservation released, output delivered -> partial billed. Guarded by 10 further cases in test_sse_keepalive.py (the sub-cadence cap fires inside its own window with no ping; the cap names itself; a consumer walking away does NOT; stamped provider activity survives a buffering hook while an unstamped one still dies; the arming rule) and 4 in test_v1_messages_client_stall.py (a buffered guardrail stream is delivered whole, a dead upstream behind the SAME buffering hook still ends, and the two terminations record different metadata). Every one falsified against the pre-revision commit or against a targeted mutation.
litellm/constants.py / litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py / litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py | STREAM_ENDED_UPSTREAM_IDLE_METADATA_KEY | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#688), the telemetry half of the upstream-idle cap in the row above and the reason that issue exists at all: streaming rows were logged HTTP 200 with a truncated body and nobody could tell, so a cap whose own firing is filed as a client disconnect rebuilds exactly that blind spot one layer up -- an operator reading 499s could not separate 'the caller went away' from 'we gave up on a dead model while the caller was still reading'. Both terminations tear down through the same generator close, so the cause has to be carried explicitly. A _StreamTermination pairs a metadata flag with its error_information: client_disconnected/499/ClientDisconnected as before, or stream_ended_upstream_idle/504/UpstreamStreamIdle (LITELLM_HTTP_STATUS_UPSTREAM_STREAM_IDLE) for the cap. _record_streaming_client_disconnect_if_needed takes the reason and skips its is_disconnected() probe when one is named, since the caller is asserting a cause rather than looking for an unreported disconnect -- which matters because on the upstream-idle path the client is typically still attached, so probing would record nothing and the reservation refund / partial-spend billing that hangs off that return value would be skipped. get_error_information_for_logging_payload honours either flag, so the standard logging payload carries 504 rather than a row with no error information at all, and the new key is added to the pre-call metadata strip list so a client can forge neither flag. Guarded by test_the_idle_cap_is_not_recorded_as_a_client_disconnect and its deliberate contrast test_a_client_that_stops_reading_is_still_recorded_as_a_client_disconnect in tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_v1_messages_client_stall.py -- the second one exists because a signal that fired on every teardown would separate nothing. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove with the cap itself (see the row above); until then do NOT 'simplify' this back to a single client_disconnected flag -- that is the defect, not the cleanup.

litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | def _failure_exception | 2026-09-24 sync brought in upstream's own new Responses WS failure-reporting mechanism (_failure_exception/_record_usage_for_failure/_ws_event_error/_RESPONSES_WS_FAILURE_EVENT_TYPES, and bidirectional_forward returning Exception | None so the caller can react to a failed connection) alongside this fork's pre-existing per-turn success-cost fix (_dispatch_turn_cost, see the RESPONSES_WS_TERMINAL_EVENT_CLASSES row above). The two are orthogonal, not competing: upstream's mechanism reports a FAILED connection's error to the connection-level logging_obj (dispatch_failure_handlers) and propagates the exception to the caller once, at connection close, while the fork's mechanism costs each completed/failed/incomplete turn as it happens via a fresh per-turn logging_obj (dispatch_success_handlers) -- restoring one is not a reason to drop the other. The first sync pass incorrectly reverted bidirectional_forward's return type back to None and dropped _failure_exception/_record_usage_for_failure entirely, reading the fork's own _log_messages docstring ("dropped entirely") as covering the whole method; that docstring's stated reason ($0 cost from dispatching a bare self.messages list, rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#657) applies only to the SUCCESS branch _log_messages used to run, never to the failure branch, which already costs a typed LiteLLMRealtimeStreamLoggingObject and was never part of that bug. Restored upstream's failure mechanism verbatim into _log_messages (the success branch stays dropped) and added the failure-dispatch task to the existing _pending_cost_tasks drain so it is not lost to the same weak-reference GC risk _dispatch_turn_cost's own tasks were fixed against. litellm/harness/endpoint.py / litellm/harness/runtime.py / litellm/constants.py | HARNESS_ENDPOINT_CONTAINER_BIND_HOST | 2026-10-03 sync, flagged by Claude Code Review on PR #293: litellm.harness's DockerSandbox tells the sandboxed runtime to reach its ModelEndpoint at http://host.docker.internal:<port> (docker.py's host_url(), resolved via --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway), but ModelEndpoint._build_server always bound uvicorn to loopback-only HARNESS_ENDPOINT_HOST ("127.0.0.1"). On native Linux Docker Engine (not Docker Desktop) that host-gateway alias resolves to the docker0 bridge IP, a different interface than loopback, so every sandboxed model call got connection-refused -- a brand-new upstream feature that never worked outside Docker Desktop, with no test catching it since tests/unit/harness/sandbox/test_docker.py mocks the docker CLI rather than exercising real host connectivity. Added an optional bind_host constructor parameter to ModelEndpoint (default unchanged: loopback) and had runtime.py's _open_endpoint pass the new 0.0.0.0 constant whenever the configured sandbox reports is_container=True; the host-side caller still connects via the unchanged, loopback-only self.url property, and every request remains gated by ModelEndpoint's own per-session bearer token regardless of which interface it arrived on. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this is upstream's own gap, so drop the sandbox-aware bind_host plumbing if upstream ships an equivalent fix itself and a sync absorbs it.
litellm/proxy/common_utils/http_parsing_utils.py | request.scope.get("type") != "http" | 2026-10-03 sync: genuine upstream breakage, byte-identical to upstream/main. This sync's own new OTLP tracing feature registers otlp_http_exception_handler as the app-wide @app.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException), which every HTTPException in the app now routes through, including ones raised while authenticating a WebSocket route (e.g. this fork's own test_realtime_websocket_refuses_the_upgrade guard, which sends no API key on purpose). The handler calls is_otlp_trace_request(request), which read request.method unconditionally -- WebSocket shares Request's HTTPConnection base (and therefore .scope) but has no .method, so every WebSocket auth failure in the whole proxy crashed with AttributeError instead of closing cleanly. Guarded on scope.get("type") before touching .method; real OTLP HTTP trace requests are unaffected since the guard only short-circuits non-HTTP connections to False. 2026-10-08 sync: this guard survived as an early `if ... != "http": return False`, functionally identical; pattern updated to match that phrasing. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this is upstream's own gap, drop the guard if upstream makes is_otlp_trace_request (or the exception handler itself) connection-type-safe and a sync absorbs it.
